title: Polish Christmas Carols: Kolędy Lyrics, Meaning and History
excerpt: Polish Christmas carols (kolędy) with first verses in Polish, plain-English meanings and pronunciation tips, plus Pasterka, carolers and the turoń.
metaDescription: Polish Christmas carols (kolędy) with first verses in Polish, plain-English meanings and pronunciation tips, plus Pasterka, carolers and the turoń.
summary: Kolędy are Polish Christmas carols, and several of the best-loved ones, like Lulajże, Jezuniu and Przybieżeli do Betlejem, are around 300 years old or more.
Bóg się rodzi, the 'queen' of Polish carols, was written by Franciszek Karpiński and published in 1792.
Chopin quoted the carol Lulajże, Jezuniu in the slow middle section of his Scherzo No. 1 in B minor.
In Polish custom kolędy are sung from the midnight Mass (Pasterka) until 2 February, when the Christmas season ends.

factNotes: Kolęda < Latin 'calendae': the ORPEG source only says 'Latin origin'; calendae is the standard etymology but I did not open a dictionary entry for it. W żłobie leży: Skarga attribution exists only in Jesuit sources (hedged 'not certain'); the polonaise-tune link is unsourced even on Wikipedia, hedged as 'some writers'. Bóg się rodzi first performance in Białystok 1792 hedged as 'tradition says'; melody origin left as uncertain (Kurpiński attribution omitted). Cicha noc Polish translator hedged: Wolne Lektury says 'translator unknown', Polish Wikipedia names Piotr Maszyński (c. 1930) for 'one version'. Dzisiaj w Betlejem refrain variant (Pan/nas oswobodzi) noted explicitly. Przybieżeli verse uses the modern church text (ORPEG / Siedlecki 1878), not the quite different 1911 Miarka text on Wolne Lektury. 'lira' rendered simply as lyre (no hurdy-gurdy claim). 'Wśród nocnej ciszy opens many midnight Masses' based on Radio Kraków + search summaries, worded as 'many parishes'. Scenario dialogue is illustrative. Featured and candle images are generic stock, not claimed to be Polish; the candle photo's sheet music is not a Polish carol and the caption doesn't say it is.
